keyQuotes: Enterprise search is challenging, because you have duplicate information, outdated information, things that seemingly look the same but every enterprise has its own nomenclature.
If the question was very simple, or the search was very simple, the parent node can just do it. It doesn't even need to come up with a plan.
The advantage of doing it as middleware is that the streaming of the answer and the citation generation happen in parallel, so you never interrupt the user.

mainPoints.explanation: The initial hardcoded sub-agent approach was replaced by a dynamic 'Global Agent' that spawns child agents at runtime, enabling flexible handling of complex, multi-step requests without predefined workflows.
mainPoints.point: Box evolved from single-file Q&A to a recursive parent/child agent architecture for enterprise-scale tasks.

mainPoints.explanation: Middleware intercepts model and tool calls to run citation generation in parallel with response streaming, implement prompt caching for multi-turn conversations, and automatically summarize context when it exceeds 170,000 tokens.
mainPoints.point: Deep Agents middleware enables parallel citation generation and efficient context management.

mainPoints.explanation: Box chose Deep Agents because it preserved the ability to offer customers a choice of LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) and accelerated engineering velocity, reducing agent shipping time from months to weeks.
mainPoints.point: Model agnosticism and speed of iteration were critical framework selection criteria.

mainPoints.explanation: All agents share the same full set of tools (BM25, vector search, structured Q&A, file operations), with the model deciding which tools to use rather than relying on static routing logic.
mainPoints.point: The architecture uses a uniform tool registry accessible to both parent and child agents.

oneSentenceSummary: This article details how Box AI built its enterprise content agent using LangChain's Deep Agents framework, employing a recursive parent/child architecture for scalable, secure, and model-agnostic document analysis.
originalTitle: How Box AI built enterprise content agents with Deep Agents
summary: The article presents a case study of Box AI's evolution from single-file Q&A to an enterprise-scale agentic system built on Deep Agents. It explains the architectural shift from hardcoded, specialized sub-agents to a recursive parent/child model where a 'Global Agent' dynamically spawns child agents to handle complex, multi-step tasks like cross-enterprise search and multi-document synthesis. Key design decisions include complete model agnosticism (supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.), the use of Deep Agents middleware for parallel citation generation, prompt caching, and context management, and a focus on engineering velocity that reduced agent shipping time from months to weeks. The article concludes with a vision for agents possessing the institutional knowledge of a long-tenured employee.
title: How Box AI built enterprise content agents with Deep Agents
